findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the skew-labeling mechanism: carry the pre-convention MISSING close_class cohort as an explicit bucket/label WITHIN the close_class-distribution value payload, not via the closed spec-level source/confidence labels.
evidence: MetricValue attaches one source+confidence to the whole value (registry.py:65-77)
AC-2 requires the MISSING cohort 'surfaced as a labeled cohort, never silently dropped or merged'
findings.finding: The plan says to 'Use the registry's source/confidence labels to flag taxonomy-window skew,' but source and confidence are CLOSED spec-level vocabularies (source∈{structural,git,sidecar,snapshot,backfill_classified}, confidence∈{high,classified}) that ride on the entire value; they cannot express a per-cohort annotation like '214 pre-convention bugs with MISSING close_class.' The skew/cohort label must be carried inside the computed value payload, not the provenance labels.
findings.location: Approach ('Use the registry's source/confidence labels to flag taxonomy-window skew')
scenarios: Author tries to encode the pre-convention cohort via a source/confidence value and finds no vocabulary member for it, or the single label cannot separate the classed vs MISSING portions of one distribution value
findings.suggested_fix: Have the close_class-distribution value include a distinct 'MISSING' (pre-convention) bucket alongside the vocabulary classes, so the cohort is a labeled key in the returned distribution.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the aggregation protocol for each dimension: the exact percentile set (e.g. p50/p90/p99), the timestamp pair for time-to-close, and the counting unit for caused_by fan-in.
evidence: 'open-bug age percentiles; caused_by link fan-in per target; time-to-close percentiles'
E2 rule: 'a derived metric with no computation or aggregation protocol' is a data-design ambiguity under signals (1)/(2)
AC line 'exposes a bug_trends lens with the five dimensions' does not pin which percentiles or the fan-in unit
findings.finding: The five dimensions name metrics but do not state their computation/aggregation protocol: which percentiles for open-bug age and time-to-close, the timestamp fields time-to-close is derived from, and what 'caused_by fan-in per target' counts (bugs, links, distinct sources).
scenarios: Executor picks p50/p90 while reviewer expected p50/p90/p99
time-to-close computed from created->closed vs first-triage->closed changes the numbers
fan-in counted per link vs per distinct source component yields different distributions
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Approach: 'age/time-to-close report p50/p90/p99; time-to-close = closed_at - created_at; caused_by fan-in = count of distinct caused-by bugs per target component; close_class buckets by close-month.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State bug_trends' range semantics explicitly: either bucket over ALL history (ignoring ctx.since/until, a deliberate deviation from sibling range-scoped metrics) or scope to the range — and justify the choice against the 'aggregate 344 closed bugs / flag 214 pre-convention' goal.
evidence: metrics_cli defaults to last-30-day since/until and passes them on ctx (metrics.py:35-45,140-148)
Problem: aggregate '344 closed bugs' and flag '214 bugs' pre-convention era
findings.finding: The plan never states whether bug_trends honors the ctx since/until range. The metrics CLI always threads a range (default last 30 days) into ctx, and existing bug/event metrics filter on it. If bug_trends respects the range, the default 30-day window excludes essentially all 344 historical closed bugs and empties the 214-bug pre-convention era-skew cohort the plan is built to surface; if it ignores the range, that deliberate deviation from every sibling metric needs to be stated.
scenarios: Default `rebar metrics` run with the 30-day window returns an empty/near-empty close_class distribution and no era-skew cohort, defeating the trend goal

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that bug_trends is registered as FIVE sibling MetricSpecs sharing lens='bug_trends' (one per dimension), matching gate_economics, so each dimension is independently MetricValue-or-Unavailable per the registry's atomic dispatch.
evidence: sidecar_metrics.register() appends 3 separate specs sharing lens='gate_economics' (sidecar_metrics.py:277-289)
AC-3: 'degrades that dimension to unavailable without affecting others'
findings.finding: AC-1 ('a bug_trends lens with the five dimensions') and AC-3 (detected_by degrades to unavailable 'without affecting others') cannot both be met if bug_trends is a single MetricSpec: the registry evaluates each spec atomically to ONE MetricValue or ONE Unavailable, with no notion of independently-unavailable sub-dimensions. The existing gate_economics lens registers one spec per derivation (cost_per_accepted_change / env_diagnosis_intervals / first_pass_verification) sharing lens='gate_economics'. The plan does not state whether bug_trends is one spec or five.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC-1 / AC-3; Approach ('same _spec() registration pattern')
scenarios: detected_by is empty everywhere but close_class/age/etc. have data — a single-spec bug_trends must either report the whole lens unavailable or bury the sub-unavailable inside a value, neither matching AC-3's per-dimension contract
findings.suggested_fix: Register five specs (bug_close_class_distribution, bug_detected_by_distribution, bug_open_age, bug_caused_by_fanin, bug_time_to_close) each with lens='bug_trends', so detected_by's compute returning None yields Unavailable for that spec alone.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-line positive rationale stating why per-dimension sibling specs on a shared lens (independent unavailability + registry-native rendering) is the right fit for aggregating heterogeneous, differently-mature bug signals.
evidence: Approach cites pattern reuse but not a fitness rationale
G6(4): absence of a POSITIVE rationale for the chosen approach is a finding
findings.finding: The Approach gives only a mechanical rationale ('same _spec() registration pattern as gate-economics') and no positive rationale for why this lens design (five distinct dimensions, per-dimension graceful degradation, in-payload cohort labeling) fits the problem better than alternatives such as a single composite value or an ad-hoc script promoted into the CLI.
scenarios: Reviewer/implementer cannot tell whether five-sibling-spec decomposition was chosen deliberately or by imitation
